name: Incline Dumbbell Reverse Fly
summary: An upper-body isolation exercise targeting the posterior deltoids and upper back while lying prone on an incline bench.

aliases.text: Prone Incline Dumbbell Rear Delt Raise

setup: Set an adjustable bench to a low incline, typically between 30 and 45 degrees.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand and lie chest-down against the bench pad.
Plant your toes firmly on the floor and let your arms hang straight down beneath your shoulders with a slight bend in the elbows.
steps: Maintaining a fixed, soft bend in the elbows, raise the dumbbells out to the sides in a wide arc.
Lift until your upper arms are roughly aligned with your torso, feeling the contraction in your rear deltoids and upper back.
Pause briefly at the peak of the movement without shrugging your shoulders toward your ears.
Lower the dumbbells under control along the same path back to the starting position.
instructions.breathing: Exhale as you raise the dumbbells out to the sides and inhale as you lower them.
cues: Keep the chest glued to the pad.
Reach out wide rather than pulling back.

common_faults.fault: Excessively bending the elbows to turn the fly into a row.
common_faults.correction: Maintain a fixed, slight bend in the elbows throughout the entire range of motion.

common_faults.fault: Lifting the chest off the bench to use momentum.
common_faults.correction: Keep your sternum pressed into the bench pad and reduce the weight if necessary.
Keep the shoulder blades depressed and focus on pulling the elbows outward away from the body.

precautions: Avoid using excessively heavy loads that compromise shoulder mechanics or cause neck strain.
